findings.F1: The top-decile rebound is mostly the whole market bouncing, not the coin itself: the mean excess over the coin's own 20-bar mean is +3.3% (median +1.5%, hit 56%, t 1.85, 108 non-overlapping episodes), but against BTC's forward 20-bar return over the same bars it is −0.15% (hit 44%, t −0.10, 91 episodes), and the coin's forward return correlates 0.72 with BTC's.
findings.F2: The effect depends heavily on the period: top-decile excess is +13.7% in 2020 (t 3.5, n 9), +7.9% in 2022 (t 2.25, n 22) and +10.5% in 2023 (t 2.06, n 10), but −6.3% in 2018 (t −1.22, n 20) and −5.3% in 2024 (t −1.37, n 11); among windows, 15 of 22 have a positive mean.
findings.F3: The rebound is limited to falls that are still running: top-decile bars whose last 5 days were also down give +4.1% (hit 58%, t 1.98, n 88), while those that had already turned up over 5 days give −0.1% (t −0.05, n 20).
findings.F4: The rebound also needs the close to sit near the bottom of its 20-day range: with the close in the lowest quarter of the high-low range it is +5.8% (n 24) and +6.2% (t 1.87, n 35), against +0.1% (t 0.04, n 36) higher in the range; with the close within the lowest third of distance from its 5-day low it is +5.4% (t 2.02, n 32).
findings.F5: Raw depth splits the result in two directions: across all non-overlapping bars, 20-day falls deeper than 20% are followed by +3.5% (n 38) and +3.9% (n 65) excess, but falls of 10–20% are followed by −5.1% (hit 34%, t −2.36, n 88).
findings.F6: Among positive forecasts, forward excess rises steadily with forecast size: from −6.6% in the lowest quintile (hit 32%, t −2.94, n 85) to +3.7% in the top quintile (t 1.73, n 85). Small standardised declines therefore keep falling, and only large ones rebound. Because 24% of positive forecasts sit at the +20 cap, the top decile cannot separate the large declines from the extreme ones.

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen more than about 20% over 20 days and is still falling over its last 5 days, closing in the bottom quarter of its 20-day range, it rises over the next 20 days by more than its usual 20-day move.
ideas.consequence: A trader buying deep monthly falls should buy only while the fall is still running near its low, and refuse falls that have already bounced or are shallower.
ideas.name: still-falling deep drop rebounds

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen a moderate 10–20% over 20 days, it keeps falling over the next 20 days by more than its usual 20-day move.
ideas.consequence: A trader should refuse to buy moderate monthly falls, and can treat them as a continuation of the down move rather than a dip to buy.
ideas.name: moderate drop keeps falling

ideas.idea: When a coin has fallen deeply over 20 days, its next 20-day return beats its usual move only in the periods when Bitcoin is also rebounding, so the coin's rise follows the market's bounce rather than its own.
ideas.consequence: A trader should judge a deep-fall long by the market's rebound and expect no gain over simply holding Bitcoin.
ideas.name: deep-drop rebound follows market
